# At-Risk Test Register (v1)

**Artifact:** `at-risk-test-register-v1.json`
**Baseline commit:** `a68c6e3`
**Owning story:** 1.3 — *Decouple the internal-coupled tests that would break under refactor*
**Generated by:** `AtRiskTestRegisterGenerationTest.GenerateAndSaveAtRiskTestRegisterFile`
(regenerate with `dotnet test tests/Hexalith.Conversations.Conformance.Tests --filter "FullyQualifiedName~AtRiskTestRegisterGenerationTest"`)

## Role

This register is the **seed of the FR-20 removed-test justification ledger** that **Story 5.2** reconciles, and an input to **Story 5.1**'s structural-survivability confirmation. It maps every internal-coupled (at-risk) test — and, where a file is split per-assertion, each at-risk assertion group — that the Conversations Boilerplate Reduction refactor (Epic 2/3) would otherwise break *for the wrong reason* (a moved internal type failing to compile, rather than a behavior breaking) to a classification, its coupling, rationale, owning Epic 2/3 story, and re-expression artifact.

**No test is deleted in Story 1.3.** Re-expressions are added to the conformance oracle; the original at-risk tests are kept in place until their owning story retires or retargets them *with the code*.

## Classifications

| Classification | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `re-express, never delete` | Behavior safety net (the governance audit-pairing test). Re-expressed against the public surface and kept forever; deleting it would silently drop a conformance behavior. |
| `re-express` | Behavior assertion whose coupling is incidental; re-expressed against the public surface here so the underlying plumbing can move freely in its owning story. |
| `plumbing-only-retire` | Assertion with no externally-observable release-gate behavior; retired **with its code** in the named owning Epic 2/3 story. Recorded so Story 5.2 reconciles every later test-count reduction. |
| `coupled-by-design-retarget-in-owning-story` | Test that must keep touching live/internal types to do its job; the owning story updates the type reference rather than dropping the test. |

## Carry-forwards folded in from Story 1.2

1. **Internal governance audit gate** — **CLOSED by Story 2.1 (AC-5 / Epic 1 retro T3)**: *surfaced, not retired*. The fail-closed-on-sink-failure behavior is live and used by the governed command handlers, so the shared host does not make it redundant. The gate stays `internal` (making it public would change the public contract shape, which the standing gate forbids); its behavior is now observable in the oracle through the **public** governed command-handler surface by `GovernanceAuditSinkFailClosedConformanceTest` — a throwing audit sink yields a fail-closed rejection (`audit_unavailable`) with no mutation event, with a contrast fact for the healthy sink. Fault-injection verified (bypassing the gate's catch turns the throwing-sink fact red).
2. **Test-parallelism race** — **CLOSED by Story 2.1 (Epic 1 retro T1)**: it recurred while running the standing gate (Epic 2 raised run frequency), so it was fixed test-only — every reader and writer of a committed `docs/release-evidence/*` artifact now shares the non-parallel `ReleaseEvidenceArtifactCollection`, so a generation test never interleaves with a validation test of the same file. No assertion strength changed; the rest of the suite stays parallel. Verified green across repeated full-suite runs.

## Story 2.3 structural dispositions (append-only, agreements A2/A3)

Recorded when Story 2.3 (FR-4, consume the platform query-handler seam + cursor codec) removed the hand-rolled HMAC continuation-cursor codec, re-expressed the HMAC-specific cursor tests against the platform codec, and confirmed the conversation-specific query surface as Keep. See `story23StructuralDispositions` in the JSON.

| Subject | Change | AC | Green after |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hand-rolled HMAC-SHA256 list continuation cursor codec (`ConversationQueryCursor`) + the crypto half of `ConversationQueryCursorOptions` (`SigningKey` / `KeyId`) | **Removed and replaced** by the platform protected-cursor codec (`IQueryCursorCodec`, ASP.NET Core Data Protection backed) + the `QueryCursorScope` binding builder. Tenant / caller / filter fingerprint / sort version bind into the scope; offset / issued-at / projection-generation token ride in the protected position; the `MaxAge` / `MaxOffset` / clock-skew guards stay as domain checks re-applied after decode. No `HMACSHA256` / `FixedTimeEquals` cursor-signing code remains under the Server query boundary. Registered once under the stable purpose `Hexalith.Conversations.QueryCursor.v1`. Public contract-shape baseline unaffected — the codec lived in the Server assembly and the cursor is an opaque `string` on the public `ConversationPageMetadata` / `ConversationListResult` Contracts surface. | AC-1 / AC-2 / AC-5 | ✅ |
| HMAC-specific cursor fail-closed tests (Tampered / DifferentKey / Expired / FutureDated / GenerationMismatched / TenantMismatched / CallerMismatched / Malformed / ExcessiveOffset) + the `ForgeCursorWithOffset` helper | **Re-expressed** against the platform codec, **not deleted**. Each still asserts the same safe Hidden / Forbidden shape; the integrity cases still assert **zero** projection reads, and the tenant/caller scope cases now **also** assert zero reads (caught at the scope boundary before any read — assertion strength **increased**). `ForgeCursorWithOffset` is rebuilt to forge via the codec position. Net-new `IssuedContinuationCursorShouldRoundTripToNextPage` + the query-seam reach tests (`ConversationDomainQueryDispatchTest`, `ExplicitAssemblyScanShouldDiscoverConversationDomainQueryHandlers`) keep the count monotonic. | AC-2 / AC-5 | ✅ |
| Conversation-specific query logic: filter dimensions, worst-case freshness aggregation, read-time hydration (citations / audit records / privileged-justification review), temporal reconstruction (`ConversationTemporalReconstructionService` + the temporal permalink / anchor contracts), and the `Contracts/Queries` DTOs | **KEEP, unchanged** (AC-4). Exposed through the platform query-handler seam (`IDomainQueryHandler`) as a **thin adapter** (`ConversationDomainQueryHandlerBase` + list/detail handlers) that deserializes the envelope, delegates to the existing `ConversationQueryHandler`, and serializes the result — reimplementing none of the filter/freshness/hydration/temporal logic. The temporal permalink/anchor path is an unsigned domain contract left untouched, so temporal cursors / permalinks re-resolve to the same position. No source edits to the reconstruction service or `Contracts/Queries`. | AC-3 / AC-4 | ✅ |
